raw_segments.text: Thus did he speak, and they did even as he had said.
The son of Tidius, Ulysses, and Agamemnon, wounded though they were, set the others in
array and went about everywhere affecting the exchanges of armor.
The most valiant took the best armor and gave the worst to the worst man.
When they had donned their bronze armor they marched on with Neptune at their head.
In his strong hand he grasped his terrible sword, keen of edge and flashing like lightning.
Woe to him who comes across it in the day of battle.
All men quake for fear and keep away from it.
